title: Learning: Classical Conditioning - Pavlov, Watson, Elements, Generalization
summary: Classical conditioning (Pavlov); before/after conditioning; elements of classical conditioning; stimulus generalization; higher-order conditioning; John Watson; Garcia effect; counter conditioning (Mary Cover Jones).
objectives: Identify elements of classical conditioning (NS, US, UR, CS, CR).
Explain stimulus generalization and higher-order conditioning.
Describe Watson's Little Albert and Garcia effect.
revision: Classical conditioning: learning through association. Elements: NS, US, UR, CS, CR. Watson's Little Albert (fear conditioning). Garcia effect = taste aversion with long delay. Counter conditioning = eliminating fear with pleasant pairing.
traps: NS → CS after pairing with US.
confusions: Believing all conditioning requires contiguity (Garcia effect exception).

notes.t: Classical conditioning is learning through association. A neutral stimulus becomes a conditioned stimulus after being paired with an unconditioned stimulus.
Stimulus generalization occurs when stimuli similar to the conditioned stimulus also elicit the conditioned response.
A neutral stimulus is paired with an already-established conditioned stimulus, becoming a second-order conditioned stimulus.
John Watson demonstrated classical conditioning in humans with Little Albert, conditioning fear of a white rat by pairing it with a loud noise.
The Garcia effect (taste aversion) shows that classical conditioning can occur with long delays between CS (taste) and US (nausea), violating contiguity.
Mary Cover Jones demonstrated counter conditioning by pairing a feared stimulus with a pleasant one to eliminate fear (e.g., Peter and the rabbit).
UGC NET frequently asks about Pavlov's elements (NS, US, UR, CS, CR), Watson's Little Albert, and the Garcia effect.

mnemonics.title: NS-US-UR-CS-CR
mnemonics.text: NS — Neutral stimulus (no response), US — Unconditioned stimulus (elicits UR), UR — Unconditioned response (natural), CS — Conditioned stimulus (elicits CR), CR — Conditioned response (learned)

flashcards.a: Learning through association (neutral stimulus paired with US).
